SAS PROBNORM(x)

Source: R/doc_functions.R
sas_f_probnorm.Rd

Standard normal cumulative probability. See the SAS documentation (Functions and CALL Routines).

Arguments

x

Numeric value at which the standard normal CDF is evaluated. Missing gives missing.

Value

A vector with one result per element (arguments are recycled), as the SAS function returns per observation.

Differences from R

Arguments and parameterisation are those of the SAS function (order of arguments, noncentrality), not those of R's d/p/q/r functions.

See also

Other probability functions: sas_f_cdf(), sas_f_cinv(), sas_f_finv(), sas_f_logcdf(), sas_f_logpdf(), sas_f_logsdf(), sas_f_pdf(), sas_f_poisson(), sas_f_probbnml(), sas_f_probchi(), sas_f_probf(), sas_f_probit(), sas_f_probt(), sas_f_quantile(), sas_f_sdf(), sas_f_tinv()

Examples

# PROBNORM: each call is explained above it and followed by its result

# PROBNORM is approximate: in strict mode (the default) a direct call stops; these calls
# run with options(sasonr.strict = FALSE) and a warning of class sasonr_strict_warning.
old <- options(sasonr.strict = FALSE)

# The standard normal CDF at 1.96 is about 0.975.
sas_f_probnorm(1.96)  # probnorm(1.96) = 0.97500210485178
#> Warning: sasonr: function PROBNORM is approximate
#> This warning is displayed once per session.
#> [1] 0.9750021

# The standard normal CDF at 0 is 0.5.
sas_f_probnorm(0)  # probnorm(0) = 0.5
#> [1] 0.5

# A missing argument gives a missing result.
sas_f_probnorm(NA_real_)  # probnorm(.) = .
#> [1] NA

options(old)
